title: wt sweep --dry-run --json
description: What wt sweep would do, and what it would keep and why. Printed by `wt sweep --dry-run --json` (or `wt sweep --json` without --yes) as the only thing on stdout; nothing is deleted. Schema 1: fields may be added and enumerations may gain values; nothing is renamed or removed. See docs/json.md.

schema.description: The major version: a new one only for a change that breaks readers.

schemaVersion.description: The full semantic version of this schema that the output follows: minor for an added field or enumeration value, patch for wording.

repo.description: The repository's main checkout; null outside one.

trunk.description: Trunk's branch name; null outside a repository.

trunkSource.description: How trunk was determined, first match wins, from local refs alone (since 1.3.0): config — MAIN_BRANCH in the wt configuration file; originHead — refs/remotes/origin/HEAD; conventional — the first of development, main, master that exists locally or on origin (since 1.4.1; before, main, master, trunk, development, develop, ranked by where each exists); currentBranchGuess — no longer produced since 1.4.1: when nothing names trunk, detection fails and the repository reports noConfiguration. Null when trunk is.

bases.description: What merged is measured against, first one first: origin/<trunk> as fetched, then <trunk>.

fetched.description: origin was fetched first (false with --no-fetch, without an origin, or when the plan stopped before).

token.description: Names this plan; pass it to `wt sweep --expect <token> --yes --json`. Null when there is nothing to remove or delete, or on error.

error.description: Why no plan could be made: not the main checkout, no trunk, the fetch failed — items is then empty — or a --move-to folder that cannot be used.

quarantine.description: Since 1.2.0. With --move-to <dir>: the folder the worktrees go to, absolute, which the token covers; a folder that exists or is on another volume refuses the plan (error set, token null, items kept). null without it.

keepSuperset.description: Since 1.4.0. --keep-superset was given: the removed worktrees' Superset workspaces are left, and Superset is not asked anything. The token covers it.

reap.description: Since 1.6.0. --reap was given: the processes still working in each worktree that goes are stopped first, and they no longer keep it. The token covers it, and the processes of each remove item.

configFingerprint.description: Since 1.5.0. The wt configuration the token covers: the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the configuration file wt read (bin/worktree/worktree.toml or worktree.conf). Two plans with the same value read the same file. null when there is none.

category.description: remove: the worktree goes, and its branch with it. delete: a branch in no worktree goes. inUse: merged, but its worktree is kept (kept says why). upstreamGone: its upstream is gone but trunk lacks its commits, kept.

tip.description: The branch's commit, or a detached worktree's HEAD.

work.description: The worktree's work name; null for a branch in no worktree, or a detached one.

path.description: The worktree; null for a branch in no worktree.

merged.description: Why it counts as merged; null for upstreamGone.

pullRequest.description: What GitHub says about the branch's pull request; null when there is none, or GitHub was not asked.

kept.description: Why it is kept, every reason that applies; empty for remove and delete. processes (since 1.6.0): without --reap, processes still run in its worktree (listed in processes). processesUnknown (since 1.6.0): the processes in it could not be found, or told apart from agent sessions.

reason.description: The row as wt sweep prints it: why it goes, or why it stays and what to do.

ahead.description: For upstreamGone: commits the first base lacks.

processes.description: Since 1.6.0. The processes working in its worktree, as remove-plan lists them: another user's, any with a controlling terminal, wt's own and agent processes are never listed. reap is true on a remove item under --reap, which stops them before the worktree goes; they keep an inUse item only without --reap, when kept has processes; under --reap, or on a row kept for another reason, they are listed and do not hold it. Empty for a branch in no worktree, and when none was found.

command.description: Its command line as ps shows it, arguments joined with spaces.

how.description: ancestor: into contains the tip. patch: every commit is on into under another id, byte for byte. pullRequest: GitHub merged its pull request into trunk at exactly this tip.

into.description: The base it is on; trunk's name for pullRequest.
